reply:
Here is the same idea in simple words.

The Graph controls the task, and each Node is one step of it. When the task reaches the point where it must wait for a confirmation, it stops there. A Checkpoint, which is a saved record of the Graph state, links the reply you send back to the step that was waiting. So when the reply arrives, the Graph continues at that same step, and the Node after it sends the report.

One thing to keep in mind: a Checkpoint does not guarantee that an external action, such as writing a file, happens only once. If the system crashes after the file write, the system cannot be sure the write happened only one time.
